content: Kurnool Medical College, located in Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh, India, is a prominent institution for medical education. When the state of Andhra was formed in October 1953, the government decided to establish a medical college in the Rayalaseema region. In Government Order Ms. No. 1835, dated November 29, 1955, the Andhra government sanctioned the establishment of the third medical college in the state at Kurnool. Since the college building was not ready, 50 students were initially admitted to Kurnool Medical College in July 1956. After the formation of Andhra Pradesh and the relocation of the state capital to Hyderabad, the former secretariat building in Kurnool was handed over to the medical college. T. Krishnamachari, the then Finance Minister of India, played a significant role in the development of the college. Laboratories for non-clinical subjects were established, and a clinical lecture hall combined with a clinical pathology laboratory was constructed. Additionally, an air-conditioned mortuary with a capacity for 24 bodies was built, and these facilities were completed by the summer of 1958. A new outpatient block for the Government General Hospital, the associated teaching hospital, was constructed at a cost of Rs. 900,000. The inauguration of this block and the clinical courses took place on January 28, 1958, by Sri D.K. Karmankar, the Health Minister of India. The first batch of 50 students, initially admitted to Guntur Medical College in July 1956, joined Kurnool Medical College for their clinical courses. The first units in major subjects such as Medicine, Surgery, and Midwifery were established in July 1957. The college was initially affiliated with Sri Venkateswara University in January 1957 and gained permanent affiliation in January 1959. An NCC unit was started in January 1958, and laboratory technician and laboratory attendant courses began in October 1959. In the same year, a Regional Laboratory was established to serve the Rayalaseema districts. In 1961, a well-planned animal house with separate units for different laboratory animals was commissioned. A Central Workshop began functioning in 1964. The legislators' hostel near the college was converted into a men's hostel in 1958, accommodating 175 students, and later expanded to house 350 students. The state guesthouse was also handed over in 1958 and repurposed as a women's hostel. Additional accommodations for women were provided in improved sheds within the hospital premises. A new extension, costing Rs. 2 crores, was nearly completed to provide accommodation for 150 more women students and 56 women postgraduate students, consolidating all women students in one location. The government sanctioned the transfer of an adjacent site to the college for use as a playground. In 1959, the Anatomy Department was expanded, and a rural health center for teaching social and preventive medicine was opened in Parla village in 1960. The college offers postgraduate degree and diploma courses, including M.Ch. in Urology. In 2003, an Acute Medical Care (AMC) unit and an Intensive Coronary Care Unit (ICCU) were established in the Government General Hospital, Kurnool. Between 2001 and 2003, examination halls with a capacity of 400 each were constructed to accommodate the increased number of students. Renovations were carried out in the Physiology and Anatomy departments, and additional hostel accommodations were provided for both men and women. Construction of a new mortuary building and a pathology laboratory was also initiated. In December 2006 and January 2007, the college celebrated its Golden Jubilee, marking 50 years of successful operation. Dr. Abdul Kalam, the then President of India, was invited to the celebrations. The college has produced several notable figures, including Dr. Nori Dattatreyudu, a world-renowned radiation oncologist and pioneer in brachytherapy. In 1979, Dr. Nori became the first physician in the United States to use a computerized brachytherapy treatment system, contributing significantly to cancer treatment through clinical research. He developed and popularized transperineal brachytherapy, a non-surgical approach for radioactive seed implantation, improving the quality of life for cancer patients. Dr. Nori, a professor and chairman of the Radiation Oncology Department at New York Presbyterian Hospital-Weill Cornell Medical Center, was honored with the Tribute to Life award by the American Cancer Society for his contributions to cancer research, patient care, and education. Other distinguished alumni include Dr. Sekhar Tam Tam, who was awarded the Member of the British Empire (MBE) in 2006 by Queen Elizabeth II for his service as District Medical Officer in Grenada, a British Caribbean island. The MBE is awarded for outstanding service or achievement within the British Empire. The college has also produced numerous other prominent figures in medicine, politics, industries, and public service, including Dr. M. Reddy, Dr. Sita Devi, Dr. K. Haranath, Dr. D. Bhaskar Reddy, Dr. B. Sadasivudu, Dr. D. Nageshwara Reddy, Dr. P. Jagannath, Dr. W. Seetharam, Dr. Mukunda Reddy, Dr. Ramakrishna Reddy, Dr. Madhubala Reddy, Dr. Babu Rao Mediyam (MP, Lok Sabha), Dr. S. Sailajanath (MLA, Singanamala, Andhra Pradesh), and Dr. Anirudh Rajaram Reddy, who works at EPMC's Women's Clinic in Bangalore.
